questions.prompt: Let $\mathbb{Z}^+$ be the set of positive integers. Determine all functions $f : \mathbb{Z}^+ \to \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that $a^2 + f(a)f(b)$ is divisible by $f(a) + b$ for all positive integers $a$ and $b$.
questions.answer: $f(n)=n$ for all $n$ (get $f(1)=1$, $b\le f(b)$ and $f(a)+1\mid a^2-1$; then $f(p)=p$ for primes $p$, and $a=p$ large forces $f(b)=b$).

questions.prompt:
Let $m$ be a fixed positive integer. The infinite sequence $\{a_n\}_{n\ge1}$ is defined in the following way: $a_1$ is a positive integer, and for every integer $n\ge1$ we have
$$a_{n+1}=\begin{cases} a_n^2+2^m & \text{if } a_n<2^m\\[2pt] a_n/2 & \text{if } a_n\ge 2^m.\end{cases}$$
For each $m$, determine all possible values of $a_1$ such that every term in the sequence is an integer.
questions.answer: Only $m=2$ admits valid starting values, and then exactly $a_1=2^\ell$ with $\ell\ge1$; for every $m\ne2$ there is no such $a_1$ (the odd parts are non-decreasing and bounded, which forces all terms to be powers of $2$).

questions.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a scalene triangle with circumcircle $\Gamma$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. A variable point $P$ is selected in the line segment $AM$. The circumcircles of triangles $BPM$ and $CPM$ intersect $\Gamma$ again at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. The lines $DP$ and $EP$ intersect (a second time) the circumcircles to triangles $CPM$ and $BPM$ at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Prove that as $P$ varies, the circumcircle of $\triangle AXY$ passes through a fixed point $T$ distinct from $A$.
questions.answer: Proof: $BY\parallel CE$ and $CX\parallel BD$ make $BCXY$ cyclic and $XY\parallel DE$; with $Q,R\in\Gamma$ such that $CQ\parallel BR\parallel AM$, the lines $DP$, $EP$ pass through $Q$, $R$ and $QRXY$ is cyclic, so $XY$ passes through the fixed point $S=BC\cap QR$ and $T$ is the second intersection of $AS$ with $\Gamma$.

questions.prompt: Consider a $2018\times 2019$ board with integers in each unit square. Two unit squares are said to be neighbours if they share a common edge. In each turn, you choose some unit squares. Then for each chosen unit square the average of all its neighbours is calculated. Finally, after these calculations are done, the number in each chosen unit square is replaced by the corresponding average. Is it always possible to make the numbers in all squares become the same after finitely many turns?
questions.answer: No. Work modulo $5$ (divisions by $2,3,4$ make sense mod $5$): reflecting the $2\times3$ block $\begin{smallmatrix}3&1&3\\0&2&0\end{smallmatrix}$ over the whole board gives a board in which every cell is already the average of its neighbours mod $5$, so it never changes mod $5$ and never becomes constant.

questions.prompt:
Determine all the functions $f : \mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that
$$f(x^2+f(y))=f(f(x))+f(y^2)+2f(xy)$$
for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.
questions.answer: $f(x)=0$ for all $x$, and $f(x)=x^2$ for all $x$ (show $f$ is even, $f(a)=f(b)\Rightarrow f(ax)=f(bx)$, then $f>0$ off $0$ and $f(1)=1$).

questions.prompt: Let $\Gamma$ be the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$. Let $D$ be a point on the side $BC$. The tangent to $\Gamma$ at $A$ intersects the parallel line to $BA$ through $D$ at point $E$. The segment $CE$ intersects $\Gamma$ again at $F$. Suppose $B, D, F, E$ are concyclic. Prove that $AC$, $BF$, $DE$ are concurrent.
questions.answer: Proof: the concyclicity forces $\angle A=\angle B$; then with $P=AC\cap BF$ the points $A,P,F,E$ are concyclic and $EP\parallel AB$, so $P$ lies on $DE$.

questions.prompt:
Show that $r=2$ is the largest real number $r$ which satisfies the following condition:

If a sequence $a_1, a_2, \ldots$ of positive integers fulfills the inequalities
$$a_n\le a_{n+2}\le\sqrt{a_n^2+ra_{n+1}}$$
for every positive integer $n$, then there exists a positive integer $M$ such that $a_{n+2}=a_n$ for every $n\ge M$.
questions.answer: Proof: for $r>2$ the sequence $a_n=a+\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ with $a\ge\frac1{r-2}$ is a counterexample; for $r=2$, $a_{n+1}\le a_n\Rightarrow a_{n+2}=a_n$ and $a_n\le a_{n+1}\Rightarrow a_{n+2}\le a_{n+1}$, so one parity class is eventually constant and the other is non-decreasing and bounded.

questions.prompt: Determine all positive integers $k$ for which there exist a positive integer $m$ and a set $S$ of positive integers such that any integer $n>m$ can be written as a sum of distinct elements of $S$ in exactly $k$ ways.
questions.answer: Exactly the powers of two, $k=2^a$ ($a\ge0$). Construction: $S=\{1,2,4,\dots\}\cup B'$ with $|B'|=a$ non-powers of $2$. Necessity: eventually $S$ is $\{x,2x,4x,\dots\}$ plus a finite set $T$, so $2^{|T|}=kx$.

questions.prompt:
Let $\mathbb{Z}$ denote the set of all integers. Find all polynomials $P(x)$ with integer coefficients that satisfy the following property:

For any infinite sequence $a_1, a_2, \ldots$ of integers in which each integer in $\mathbb{Z}$ appears exactly once, there exist indices $i<j$ and an integer $k$ such that $a_i+a_{i+1}+\cdots+a_j=P(k)$.
questions.answer: Exactly the polynomials of degree $1$: $P(x)=cx+d$ with $c,d\in\mathbb{Z}$, $c\ne0$ (pigeonhole on prefix sums mod $c$; for other degrees the values of $P$ have arbitrarily long gaps, which lets one build a bad sequence two terms at a time).

questions.prompt: Let $n\ge3$ be a fixed integer. The number $1$ is written $n$ times on a blackboard. Below the blackboard, there are two buckets that are initially empty. A move consists of erasing two of the numbers $a$ and $b$, replacing them with the numbers $1$ and $a+b$, then adding one stone to the first bucket and $\gcd(a,b)$ stones to the second bucket. After some finite number of moves, there are $s$ stones in the first bucket and $t$ stones in the second bucket, where $s$ and $t$ are positive integers. Find all possible values of the ratio $\frac{t}{s}$.
questions.answer: All rational numbers in $[1,\,n-1)$. (Upper bound: the weighted sum $q=\sum(k-1)a_k$ grows at least as fast as $t$; construction: build $a^{n-1}$ recursively and then add $1$'s.)

questions.prompt:
Prove that for each real number $r>2$, there are exactly two or three positive real numbers $x$ satisfying the equation $x^2=r\lfloor x\rfloor$.

Note: $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the largest integer less than or equal to $x$.
questions.answer: Proof: a solution is $x=\sqrt{rk}$ with $k=\lfloor x\rfloor$, and $k^2\le rk<(k+1)^2$ forces $k\in(r-3,r]$ (at most three integers), while every integer $k\in[r-2,r]$ (at least two) gives a solution.

questions.prompt: For a polynomial $P$ and a positive integer $n$, define $P_n$ as the number of positive integer pairs $(a,b)$ such that $a<b\le n$ and $|P(a)|-|P(b)|$ is divisible by $n$. Determine all polynomials $P$ with integer coefficients such that $P_n\le 2021$ for all positive integers $n$.
questions.answer: $P(x)=x+d$ with $d\ge-2022$, and $P(x)=-x+d$ with $d\le2022$ (integers $d$). Key lemma: $P(1),\dots,P(n)$ must be distinct mod $n$ for every $n$.

questions.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic convex quadrilateral and $\Gamma$ be its circumcircle. Let $E$ be the intersection of the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$, let $L$ be the center of the circle tangent to sides $AB$, $BC$, and $CD$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of the arc $BC$ of $\Gamma$ not containing $A$ and $D$. Prove that the excenter of triangle $BCE$ opposite $E$ lies on the line $LM$.
questions.answer: Proof: with $N$ the excenter, $\angle MBL=90^\circ-\frac{\gamma}2=\angle BCN$ and $\angle MCL=\angle CBN$; if $BM$, $CM$ meet circle $BCL$ again at $X$, $Y$, then triangles $BCN$ and $XYL$ have parallel sides, so the homothety centred at $M$ taking $B\to X$, $C\to Y$ takes $N\to L$.

questions.prompt:
Given a $32\times32$ table, we put a mouse (facing up) at the bottom left cell and a piece of cheese at several other cells. The mouse then starts moving. It moves forward except that when it reaches a piece of cheese, it eats a part of it, turns right, and continues moving forward. We say that a subset of cells containing cheese is good if, during this process, the mouse tastes each piece of cheese exactly once and then falls off the table. Show that:

(a) No good subset consists of $888$ cells.

(b) There exists a good subset consisting of at least $666$ cells.
questions.answer: (a) At most $3$ cheese steps in a row and each empty cell is entered at most twice, so $888$ cheeses need at least $148$ empty cells: $1036>1024$. (b) A recursive "turn-left" tile $L_i$ and "crossing" tile $X_i$ of side $2^i$ with $|L_{i+1}|=4|L_i|-1$ gives $683$ cheeses on the $32\times32$ board.

questions.prompt: Determine all functions $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ such that $f(f(a)-b)+bf(2a)$ is a perfect square for all integers $a$ and $b$.
questions.answer: (1) $f(n)=0$ for every even $n$ and $f(n)$ an arbitrary perfect square for every odd $n$; (2) $f(n)=n^2$ for all $n$.

questions.prompt:
Find all pairs $(a,b)$ of positive integers such that $a^3$ is a multiple of $b^2$ and $b-1$ is a multiple of $a-1$.

Note: An integer $n$ is said to be a multiple of an integer $m$ if there is an integer $k$ such that $n=km$.
questions.answer: Exactly the pairs $(n,n)$ and $(n,1)$, $n\ge1$ (write $a^3=b^2c$; reducing mod $a-1$ gives $c\equiv1$, then compare sizes).

questions.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a right triangle with $\angle B=90^\circ$. Point $D$ lies on the line $CB$ such that $B$ is between $D$ and $C$. Let $E$ be the midpoint of $AD$ and let $F$ be the second intersection point of the circumcircle of $\triangle ACD$ and the circumcircle of $\triangle BDE$. Prove that as $D$ varies, the line $EF$ passes through a fixed point.
questions.answer: Proof: the fixed point is the reflection $P$ of $C$ in $B$. If $EF$ meets circle $ACD$ again at $G$, then $AG\parallel DC$ (since $EB=ED$), and the half-turn about $E$ maps $G$ to the point $P$ on line $DC$ with $DP=AG$.

questions.prompt:
Find all positive integers $k<202$ for which there exists a positive integer $n$ such that
$$\left\{\frac{n}{202}\right\}+\left\{\frac{2n}{202}\right\}+\cdots+\left\{\frac{kn}{202}\right\}=\frac k2,$$
where $\{x\}$ denote the fractional part of $x$.

Note: $\{x\}$ denotes the real number $k$ with $0\le k<1$ such that $x-k$ is an integer.

Let $n$ and $k$ be positive integers. Cathy is playing the following game. There are $n$ marbles and $k$ boxes, with the marbles labelled $1$ to $n$. Initially, all marbles are placed inside one box. Each turn, Cathy chooses a box and then moves the marble with the smallest label, say $i$, to either any empty box or the box containing marble $i+1$. Cathy wins if at any point there is a box containing only marble $n$.

Determine all pairs of integers $(n,k)$ such that Cathy can win this game.
questions.answer: Cathy can win exactly when $n\le 2^{k-1}$ (build the win for $2^k$ marbles from two copies of the win for $2^{k-1}$; for $2^{k-1}+1$ marbles, induct on $k$ using the last time marble $2^{k-2}+1$ leaves the starting box).

questions.prompt: Let $a, b, c, d$ be real numbers such that $a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=1$. Determine the minimum value of $(a-b)(b-c)(c-d)(d-a)$ and determine all values of $(a,b,c,d)$ such that the minimum value is achieved.
questions.answer: The minimum is $-\frac18$, attained exactly at the $8$ quadruples obtained from $\left(\frac{1+\sqrt3}4,\,-\frac{1+\sqrt3}4,\,\frac{1-\sqrt3}4,\,-\frac{1-\sqrt3}4\right)$ by cyclic shifts and by changing all signs.

questions.prompt:
Let $n\ge5$ be an integer. Consider $n$ squares with side lengths $1,2,\ldots,n$, respectively. The squares are arranged in the plane with their sides parallel to the $x$ and $y$ axes. Suppose that no two squares touch, except possibly at their vertices.

Show that it is possible to arrange these squares in a way such that every square touches exactly two other squares.
questions.answer: Construction: split $1,\dots,n-4$ into sets $A$, $B$ with $\sum A-\sum B\in\{1,2\}$; chain each set corner-to-corner along two parallel diagonal lines and close the cycle with the squares $n-3,n$ at one end and $n-2,n-1$ at the other.

questions.prompt: Find all integers $n$ satisfying $n\ge2$ and $\dfrac{\sigma(n)}{p(n)-1}=n$, in which $\sigma(n)$ denotes the sum of all positive divisors of $n$, and $p(n)$ denotes the largest prime divisor of n.

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram. Let $W$, $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be points on sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$, respectively, such that the incenters of triangles $AWZ$, $BXW$, $CYX$ and $DZY$ form a parallelogram. Prove that $WXYZ$ is a parallelogram.
questions.answer: Proof: signed distances to the sides give $r_1+r_4=r_2+r_3$ and $r_1+r_2=r_3+r_4$, so opposite corner triangles have equal inradii; since in a triangle with fixed apex angle and inradius one leg grows exactly when the other shrinks, $AZ>CX$ leads around the parallelogram to $CX>AZ$; so $AZ=CX$, $AW=CY$ and $WXYZ$ is symmetric about the centre.

questions.prompt:
Let $c>0$ be a given positive real and $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ be the set of all positive reals. Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}_{>0}\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that
$$f((c+1)x+f(y))=f(x+2y)+2cx\quad\text{for all } x,y\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}.$$
questions.answer: $f(x)=2x$ only (first $f(y)\ge2y$ by making the two arguments equal; then $g=f-2x\ge0$ satisfies $g(z)\ge2m\,g(y)$ for $z>2y$ and all $m$).

questions.prompt:
There are $n$ line segments on the plane, no three intersecting at a point, and each pair intersecting once in their respective interiors. Tony and his $2n-1$ friends each stand at a distinct endpoint of a line segment. Tony wishes to send Christmas presents to each of his friends as follows:

First, he chooses an endpoint of each segment as a "sink". Then he places the present at the endpoint of the segment he is at. The present moves as follows:

* If it is on a line segment, it moves towards the sink.
* When it reaches an intersection of two segments, it changes the line segment it travels on and starts moving towards the new sink.

If the present reaches an endpoint, the friend on that endpoint can receive their present. Prove Tony can send presents to exactly $n$ of his $2n-1$ friends.
questions.answer: Proof: number the endpoints $1,\dots,2n$ around a circle starting from Tony; then the chords join $k$ and $k+n$. Present paths are non-crossing and match sources to sinks, so Tony's present always lands on an even-numbered endpoint; with sinks $k+1,\dots,k+n$ it lands on $2k$.

questions.prompt: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Let $D$ be a point on side $AB$ and $E$ be a point on side $AC$ such that lines $BC$ and $DE$ are parallel. Let $X$ be an interior point of $BCED$. Suppose rays $DX$ and $EX$ meet side $BC$ at points $P$ and $Q$, respectively such that both $P$ and $Q$ lie between $B$ and $C$. Suppose that the circumcircles of triangles $BQX$ and $CPX$ intersect at a point $Y\ne X$. Prove that points $A$, $X$, and $Y$ are collinear.
questions.answer: Proof: if $AX$ meets $DE$ at $Z'$ and $BC$ at $Z$, the homotheties at $A$ and at $X$ give $\frac{BZ}{ZC}=\frac{DZ'}{Z'E}=\frac{PZ}{ZQ}$, so $ZB\cdot ZQ=ZC\cdot ZP$ and $Z$ lies on the radical axis $XY$.

questions.prompt: Consider a $100\times100$ table, and identify the cell in row $a$ and column $b$, $1\le a,b\le100$, with the ordered pair $(a,b)$. Let $k$ be an integer such that $51\le k\le99$. A $k$-knight is a piece that moves one cell vertically or horizontally and $k$ cells to the other direction; that is, it moves from $(a,b)$ to $(c,d)$ such that $(|a-c|,|b-d|)$ is either $(1,k)$ or $(k,1)$. The $k$-knight starts at cell $(1,1)$, and performs several moves. A sequence of moves is a sequence of cells $(x_0,y_0)=(1,1)$, $(x_1,y_1)$, $(x_2,y_2)$, $\ldots$, $(x_n,y_n)$ such that, for all $i=1,2,\ldots,n$, $1\le x_i,y_i\le100$ and the $k$-knight can move from $(x_{i-1},y_{i-1})$ to $(x_i,y_i)$. In this case, each cell $(x_i,y_i)$ is said to be reachable. For each $k$, find $L(k)$, the number of reachable cells.
questions.answer: $L(k)=100^2-(2k-100)^2$ if $k$ is even, and $L(k)=\frac{100^2-(2k-100)^2}{2}$ if $k$ is odd (the central $(2k-100)\times(2k-100)$ square is unreachable; for odd $k$ only the colour of $(1,1)$ is reachable).

questions.prompt:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$ be positive real numbers. Prove that
$$\sum_{i=1}^n\frac1{2^i}\left(\frac2{1+a_i}\right)^{2^i}\ge\frac{2}{1+a_1a_2\cdots a_n}-\frac1{2^n}.$$
questions.answer: Proof: the lemma $\left(\frac2{1+x}\right)^{2^k}+\left(\frac2{1+y}\right)^{2^k}\ge2\left(\frac2{1+xy}\right)^{2^{k-1}}$ (base case $k=1$ is $xy(x-y)^2+(xy-1)^2\ge0$, then induct with $2(A^2+B^2)\ge(A+B)^2$) lets the sum plus $\frac1{2^n}$ telescope from $i=n$ down to $i=1$.

questions.prompt: Prove that for every positive integer $t$ there is a unique permutation $a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_{t-1}$ of $0,1,\ldots,t-1$ such that, for every $0\le i\le t-1$, the binomial coefficient $\dbinom{t+i}{2a_i}$ is odd and $2a_i\ne t+i$.
questions.answer: Proof: by Lucas/Kummer, $\binom{N}{m}$ is odd iff the binary $1$-bits of $m$ are among those of $N$; a bit-count identity forces $t+i-2a_i$ to be a single bit of $t+i$, which fixes $a_i=\frac{t+i-1}2$ for odd $t+i$ and reduces the rest to a unique "delete one bit" matching of $\{\lceil t/2\rceil,\dots,t-1\}$ with $\{0,\dots,\lfloor t/2\rfloor-1\}$, proved by induction using the largest power of $2$ below $t$ and bit complements.

questions.prompt: Line $\ell$ intersects sides $BC$ and $AD$ of cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ in its interior points $R$ and $S$ respectively, and intersects ray $DC$ beyond point $C$ at $Q$, and ray $BA$ beyond point $A$ at $P$. Circumcircles of the triangles $QCR$ and $QDS$ intersect at $N\ne Q$, while circumcircles of the triangles $PAS$ and $PBR$ intersect at $M\ne P$. Let lines $MP$ and $NQ$ meet at point $X$, lines $AB$ and $CD$ meet at point $K$ and lines $BC$ and $AD$ meet at point $L$. Prove that point $X$ lies on line $KL$.
questions.answer: Proof: $M$, $N$ and the Miquel point $E$ of $ABCD$ are Miquel points of complete quadrilaterals; $E\in KL$, $MNQP$ is cyclic, and angle chasing shows that $NQ$ and $MP$ meet $KL$ on the circle $EMN$, which meets $KL$ in only one point besides $E$.

questions.prompt: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle inscribed in a circle $\Gamma$. Let $A_1$ be the orthogonal projection of $A$ onto $BC$ so that $AA_1$ is an altitude. Let $B_1$ and $C_1$ be the orthogonal projections of $A_1$ onto $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Point $P$ is such that quadrilateral $AB_1PC_1$ is convex and has the same area as triangle $ABC$. Is it possible that $P$ strictly lies in the interior of circle $\Gamma$? Justify your answer.
questions.answer: No. If $D$ is the point of $\Gamma$ diametrically opposite $A$, then $B_1C_1\perp AD$ and $[AB_1DC_1]=\tfrac12\,AD\cdot B_1C_1=[ABC]$, so $P$ must lie on the tangent to $\Gamma$ at $D$.

questions.prompt: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be positive real numbers. Emerald makes a trip in the coordinate plane, starting off from the origin $(0, 0)$. Each minute she moves one unit up or one unit to the right, restricting herself to the region $|x - y| < 2025$ in the coordinate plane. By the time she visits a point $(x, y)$ she writes down the integer $\lfloor x\alpha + y\beta\rfloor$ on it. It turns out that Emerald wrote each non-negative integer exactly once. Find all the possible pairs $(\alpha, \beta)$ for which such a trip would be possible.
questions.answer: All pairs of positive reals with $\alpha+\beta=2$ (the numbers written must be $0,1,2,\dots$ in order, which forces $\alpha+\beta=2$; then the zigzag path along $y=x$ works).

questions.prompt: Let $P(x)$ be a non-constant polynomial with integer coefficients such that $P(0) \neq 0$. Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots$ be an infinite sequence of integers such that $P(i - j)$ divides $a_i - a_j$ for all distinct positive integers $i, j$. Prove that the sequence $a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots$ must be constant, that is, $a_n$ equals a constant $c$ for all positive integers $n$.
questions.answer: Proof: there are infinitely many primes $p$ with $p\mid P(k)$, $p\nmid k$ for some $k\ge1$; for such $p$ the sequence $a_i \bmod p$ has periods $k$ and $k+p$, hence period $\gcd(k,k+p)=1$, so $a_{i+1}-a_i$ has infinitely many prime divisors and is $0$.

questions.prompt:
Let $n \ge 3$ be an integer. There are $n$ cells on a circle, and each cell is assigned either $0$ or $1$. There is a rooster on one of these cells, and it repeats the following operation:

- If the rooster is on a cell assigned $0$, it changes the assigned number to $1$ and moves to the next cell counterclockwise.
- If the rooster is on a cell assigned $1$, it changes the assigned number to $0$ and moves to the cell after the next cell counterclockwise.

Prove that the following statement holds after sufficiently many operations:

> If the rooster is on a cell $C$, then the rooster would go around the circle exactly three times, stopping again at $C$. Moreover, every cell would be assigned the same number as it was assigned right before the rooster went around the circle $3$ times.
questions.answer: Proof: unwrap the rooster's position to an increasing integer sequence; eventually, in any three consecutive laps, each cell is stopped on exactly twice and skipped once (such a pattern exists somewhere and propagates to the next cell), which makes the whole process periodic with period three laps.

questions.prompt:
Consider an infinite sequence $a_1, a_2, \dots$ of positive integers such that
$$100!\,(a_m + a_{m+1} + \cdots + a_n)\quad\text{is a multiple of}\quad a_{n-m+1}\,a_{n+m}$$
for all positive integers $m, n$ such that $m \le n$.

Prove that the sequence is either bounded or linear.

*Observation:* A sequence of positive integers is *bounded* if there exists a constant $N$ such that $a_n < N$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. A sequence is *linear* if $a_n = n \cdot a_1$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$.
questions.answer: Proof: with $c=100!$ derive $a_{m+n}\mid c(a_m+a_n)$ and $a_{m-n}\mid c(a_m-a_n)$, so $\operatorname{lcm}(a_m,a_n)\mid c(a_{m+n}-a_m-a_n)$. If some $\operatorname{lcm}(a_m,a_n)>c^2(a_m+a_n)$, this forces additivity along progressions and then $a_k=ka_1$; otherwise a large prime power divides all big terms and hence (after removing a common factor) every term, a contradiction unless the sequence is bounded.

questions.prompt:
Find all quadruples of positive integers $(a, p, m, o)$ with $o \ge 2$ such that
$$a! + p! = m^o + 26.$$

Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Let $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_{2^n}$ be the $2^n$ subsets of an $n$-element set in some order. Prove that
$$|A_1 \cap A_2| + |A_2 \cap A_3| + \cdots + |A_{2^n-1} \cap A_{2^n}| + |A_{2^n} \cap A_1| \ge 2^{n-2}.$$
questions.answer: Proof: for each element $x$, the number of consecutive pairs both containing $x$ equals the number both missing $x$, so the sum equals $\frac12\sum_i\bigl(|A_i\cap A_{i+1}|+|\overline{A_i\cup A_{i+1}}|\bigr)$; a term is $0$ only if $A_{i+1}=\overline{A_i}$, and two consecutive terms cannot both be $0$.

questions.prompt:
Let $\mathbb{R}_+$ denote the set of positive real numbers. Determine all the functions $f : \mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}_+$,
$$|x - y| < |y - z| \quad\text{if and only if}\quad |f(x) - f(y)| < |f(y) - f(z)|.$$
questions.answer: $f(x)=ax+b$ with real constants $a\ne0$ and $b$ ($f$ is injective and satisfies Jensen's midpoint equation, so it is linear on dyadic rationals; comparing distances then pins down every value).

questions.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with an incircle $\omega$ of centre $I$. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at $E$. Let $J$ be the incentre of triangle $ABD$. The extension of the ray $EJ$ intersects $\omega$ at $P$. Prove that $PI \perp BD$.
questions.answer: Proof: the incircles of $ABD$ and $CBD$ touch $BD$ at the same point $S$; homotheties at $A$ and $C$ and the angles at $B$ give, in coordinates with origin $S$ and $BD$ as $x$-axis, that the endpoint of the diameter of $\omega$ perpendicular to $BD$ on $A$'s side is $E+\mu(J-E)$ with $\mu=\frac{2r}{r_1+r_2}>1$.

questions.prompt:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. There exist $n(n+1)$ rooms arranged in an $(n+1) \times n$ grid. For each two adjacent rooms, there is a door between them. Find the number of ways to choose a subset of doors and lock them such that there are two rooms $S$ and $G$ satisfying the following properties:

1. $S$ is in the first row and $G$ is in the $(n+1)$-th row.
2. One can reach $G$ from $S$ only through unlocked doors.
questions.answer: $2^{2n^2-2}$ (the doors inside the first and last rows are irrelevant; for the other $2n^2-2n+1$ doors, planar duality shows that exactly half of the choices allow a crossing).
